column2: Without being told, Aki Kawamura let go and stood up on her own.
{n2} sat up, smoothed her hair and clothes a little, and began to speak.
“...I'm with Japan's counterintelligence service.{r}{p}Officially, of course, it doesn't exist.”
“And this man?”
Keiko Kitano asked.
“...He has nothing to do with it.{r}{p}We just brought him along as camouflage.”
“Then why did he kill her!”
She showed an anger quite unbecoming of a professional.
“He couldn't have killed her.{r}{p}When I came to this room last night, he was completely out cold from the drug your friend gave him.{r}{p}Somebody else killed her.”
“Isn't it common sense to suspect whoever found the body first?”
When Aki Kawamura said it spitefully, {n2} shrugged.
“Suspect me if you like.{r}{p}But think hard about whether Japan would gain anything by killing her.”
At {n2}'s words, the office ladies...
no, the French spies, actually, exchanged glances.
A moment later I felt the hostile air ease, and knew the immediate danger had passed.
“Then who's the man in that closet?”
He seemed to have been searching the room before we got here.
Then he came back and hurriedly hid in the bathroom, probably.
“...CIA, most likely.”
“...Where on earth is the 'Kamaitachi'?”
“I'd like to know that myself.”
After a heavy silence, Aki Kawamura spoke.
“...When all this is over, will you give her a proper burial?”
She seemed to mean the body in the bathroom.
{n2} nodded.
Just then, there was a knock.
“Uh-oh!
Hide in the bathroom!”
{n2} whispered.
The two had already moved before she finished.
After seeing the bathroom door close, {n2} opened the door.
Midori stood there.
She looked surprised to see {n2}.
so you're here.{r}{p}I can't find the Bo...
the owner anywhere. Do you know where he went?”
“No.
Doesn't Kyoko know?”
“She doesn't.”
Had something terrible happened...?
I could feel that feeling spreading between the two of them.
“I'll help you look.{r}{p}...What about you, {n1}?”
{n2} asked.
I thought for a moment and answered.
“I'll stay here.”
“Okay...
then leave the rest to me.”
{n2} nodded, left the room, and closed the door.
After confirming through the door that their footsteps had gone down the stairs, I opened the bathroom door.
“Okay,
now's your chance.”
But just as the two inside were about to come out, there was another knock.
Again I hurriedly shut the door.
“Who is it?”
“Um, excuse me,
I'd like to ask you something
if I could...”
A faint woman's voice.
Wondering who it was, I eased the door open, and it was Mrs. Kayama.
“W-what is it?”
“Actually...”
As she said this, she held out her right hand.
Thinking she was about to hand me something, I looked down and saw her gripping what looked like a big lighter.
No, it wasn't a lighter.
It was a tiny pistol that would fit entirely inside a man's hand.
“Don't make a sound.”
She pressed the muzzle against the center of my chest and stepped into the room.
I raised both hands high and backed up two or three steps.
Mrs. Kayama closed the door behind her.
what is this supposed to be?”
“You know perfectly well.”
She said it with a chilling smile.
I-
I don't know anything.{r}{p}I have nothing to do with this.{r}{p}Really.”
I realized I had slipped up yet again.
“Oh?
Nothing to do with what, exactly?”
“Well...
that is...”
“You're not the 'Kamaitachi,' are you?{r}{p}Who do you work for?”
She, too, was one of those hunting the 'Kamaitachi'!
I was past shock and just stunned.
Her nose twitched, and she suddenly said:
“...The smell of blood?”
Keeping the muzzle on me, she shuffled toward the back of the room.
Before long she seemed to have found the bloodstain on the floor.
“Somebody was killed here, weren't they?{r}{p}And with a face that wouldn't hurt a fly...
I almost fell for it myself.”
Pushed by the pistol, I fell backward onto the bed.
“No!
That's not it!”
I couldn't stand being taken for a murderer, and found myself protesting.
“I'm not the police, you know. No need to get so worked up.{r}{p}...Come to think of it, there's one young girl I haven't seen today, have I?”
She looked slowly around the room and her eyes stopped on the closet.
“Maybe she's hiding in there?”
Cold sweat ran down me, but I was starting to think whatever happens, happens.
Keeping her attention on me, she walked to the closet and put her hand on the curtain.
The next moment the door burst open and {n2} rushed in.
Uncle's...”
{n2} froze, staring at the muzzle pointed at her.
She looked as if she couldn't believe what was happening.
For a moment, the muzzle swung back and forth between the two of us.
I considered leaping at her to grab the pistol, but I lacked the courage to take such a risk.
“What about Uncle?”
Mrs. Kayama asked, still smiling.
What is going on? Who is this woman?”
{n2} advanced, shrieking hysterically.
“Don't move!
You'll get hurt.”
{n2} ignored her sharp warning.
“Oh, please.
A model gun? How silly.{r}{p}{n1},
don't tell me you've been cheating on me with this old hag.”
She advanced on me as she said it.
“Huh?
Huh?
W-what are you talking about?
Cheating?”
“It's not a model gun! Don't come any closer!”
I thought I heard bewilderment and a trace of fear in Mrs. Kayama's voice.
She didn't want to shoot.
Of course not.
She couldn't afford to cause a commotion here.
{n2} snorted and walked up to her.
“Playing with fire is fine, but pick someone your own age.{r}{p}Honestly...”
The next moment, {n2}'s body was spinning.
At the same time a bang like a firecracker rang out, and a breeze grazed my cheek.
I couldn't tell what had happened.
Mrs. Kayama was crouched, clutching her wrist, and the pistol was nowhere to be seen.
Apparently {n2} had launched a roundhouse kick too fast for the eye to follow.
But...
what about that breeze just now?
I felt something trickle down my cheek and touched it with a finger.
Blood.
The bullet that grazed my cheek seemed to have cut the skin.
Are you okay?”
{n2} peered anxiously at my face.
“Yeah.
Just a scratch.”
I answered with a laugh
...and that's where I lost consciousness.
When I came to, I was lying on the bed with {n2} looking down at me.
“You're awake.
Thank goodness.”
“Wh-where is she?
Mrs. Kayama?”
“I had her wait in there.”
{n2} tilted her head toward the closet.
“But in there...”
“It's fine.
They're both unconscious.”
Unbelievable.
Two knocked-out spies in the closet, and one corpse with its throat slashed in the bathroom.
“Come to think of it, did the two in the bathroom go home?”
“Of course not.{r}{p}Now that we know who the 'Kamaitachi' is, we're not letting them go free.”
“What?
W-what do you mean?”
Startled, I sat bolt upright.
“I pumped sleeping gas in through the gap under the door.{r}{p}I rigged the door so it won't open, too. All that's left is to catch the 'Kamaitachi.'”
“Catch him? Who on earth is it?”
{n2} gave me a look that said, you're so slow.
“If the Kayamas aren't the 'Kamaitachi' either, the only one left is that Tanaka, right?”
“Well, that's true, but...”
“While everyone's asleep, we make the 'Kamaitachi' ours.{r}{p}Come on, let's go!”
{n2} grabbed my hand and dragged me out of the room.
“By the way, did you find Mr. Kobayashi?{r}{p}Weren't you looking for him?”
When I suddenly remembered and asked, {n2}'s expression stiffened.
“...I can't find him.{r}{p}Something bad seems to have happened.”
“Something bad...”
I fell silent.
Best not to say anything ominous.
Most of the enemy were asleep in my room, and we had plenty of allies: Toshio, Midori, and Kyoko.
Even without Mr. Kobayashi, there was probably nothing to worry about.
{n2} seemed to think so too, and without hesitating she went to Mr. Tanaka's door and knocked.
“Yes?”
A voice that sounded completely unguarded answered, and the door opened.
Even indoors he still wore his black sunglasses, and a hat on top of that.
{n2} said with a bright smile:
“Could we talk to you for a moment?”
He slowly looked back and forth between me and {n2}, then shrugged and said:
“Come in.”
Maybe he had guessed his cover was blown and was half resigned to it...
With that thought, I went in.
Noticing the notebook open on his writing desk, he hurriedly lunged for it and shut it.
“So?
What can I do for you?”
he asked, a little flustered.
“First, let me say we already know exactly who you are.”
When {n2} said it with total confidence, he showed obvious alarm.
But he was a pro, after all, and recovered his composure at once.
“...I see.
Then it can't be helped.{r}{p}So?
What do you propose?”
“A deal, of course.”
“A deal?
...Ah, you're from around here, aren't you.”
He seemed to mean she was on the Japanese side.
{n2} nodded.
Mr. Tanaka...
no, the 'Kamaitachi' gave a bold grin
and lay back on the bed.
“A deal, huh.{r}{p}And what do you plan to trade with? Money?”
“Everyone needs money, don't they?”
{n2} said.
“Of course, of course.
Everybody needs money...{r}{p}Nice line, sister.{r}{p}So?
Just how much can you folks put up?”
“Whatever amount you want.”
“Whatever?”
“Yes.”
He licked his lips and seemed to think it over.
Then a voice came from behind.
“Mind if we join in that deal, too?”
I turned around and there in the open doorway stood Mr. Kayama and his wife.
“Nobody move!”
Mrs. Kayama's sharp voice stopped {n2}, who had started to move fast.
A far bigger pistol than before, with a silencer...
no, something like a machine gun, aimed squarely at {n2}.
“This time it's no bluff.{r}{p}Move even an inch and we'll be picking up pieces of you off the floor.”
For such a mild-looking woman, she said terrifying things.
“W-w-
who are you people?! Get out!”
The 'Kamaitachi' was shouting in apparent shock.
Mr. Kayama grinned and shut the door, then spoke to the 'Kamaitachi.'
“No use playin' dumb now.{r}{p}Jus' take the same deal these two just offered ya, same as it is.{r}{p}...Only the other party ain't them,
it's us, that's all.”
The 'Kamaitachi' didn't answer, and {n2} cut in.
“A silenced Uzi submachine gun, no less. Are you Mossad planning to start a war?”
Mossad?
Isn't that something on the menu at an Indian restaurant...?
“That's samosa!”
{n2} shot back as if she had read my mind.
“Mossad is Israeli intelligence.”
Israeli intelligence?!
But Mr. Kayama said with a grin.
“Couldn't it be that they're carryin'
an Uzi on purpose, just to make it look like Israel?”
My head was in no state to think anything through calmly anymore.
Something was thrown heavily at my feet.
I looked down: a bundle of plastic rope.
“Use that to tie her up.”
me?”
“Yes.
I'll check later, so if you cut corners, be ready to get hurt.”
“Hurt...”
When I murmured it, her eyes lit up.
“Let's see...
shooting out a kneecap might be fun.{r}{p}Or else...”
I never got to hear her second idea.
The bathroom door suddenly flew open and a shadow leaped out.
Mrs. Kayama grappled with the shadow, and the machine gun clattered to the floor.
By the time I thought of picking it up, someone's hand had already reached it and was aiming it at us again.
“You tricked us earlier, didn't you.”
I slowly looked up, and the one glaring at us with burning anger was Aki Kawamura.
Pinning Mrs. Kayama to the floor, of course, was Keiko Kitano.
But they were supposed to be locked in my bathroom...
Either way, neither looked like a savior.
how did you...?”
When I managed that much, Aki Kawamura grinned.
“It looked like you'd rigged the door from outside, but luckily, the bathroom ceiling space connects to the next room.”
So the two had crawled through the ceiling.
what in the world is going on?!”
A cry of anguish rang out, and everyone turned.
The 'Kamaitachi'...
Mr. Tanaka had squeezed between the wall and the bed, trembling as he screamed.
“That's the 'Kamaitachi'?
...He looks pretty unreliable.”
Keiko Kitano, rising after her scuffle with Mrs. Kayama, said doubtfully.
Mrs. Kayama lay limp, but Mr. Kayama was quietly moving to help her up, so she didn't seem to be dead.
“Anyway, let's get him out of here fast.{r}{p}Go back to the room and call our pickup.{r}{p}I'll keep watch on these people here.”
Aki Kawamura said, still holding the machine gun,
and Keiko Kitano slipped quickly out of the room.
A pickup...
So allies really were lurking nearby.
It looked like the 'Kamaitachi' was about to fall into French hands.
As for me, I figured whatever became of the 'Kamaitachi,' I'd be happy just to get out of here alive.
But naturally, {n2} felt differently.
She said it through gritted teeth.
“If you think you're getting out of here, you're sorely mistaken.”
“Oh?
And you think you can stop us?”
Aki Kawamura sneered.
“One word over the radio and SDECE's elite unit comes running.{r}{p}Even a hundred men from the JCIA or the Cabinet Research Office wouldn't be a match.”
Bitter as it was, it was probably true; {n2} bit her lip and stayed silent.
“If you can get through,
that is.”
The voice came from beyond the door.
Aki Kawamura waved the machine gun and ordered Mr. Kayama to open the door.
Mr. Kayama reluctantly opened it.
There stood Keiko Kitano with a pistol pressed to her temple.
Behind her, holding the pistol, was Midori.
hurry up and take that dangerous toy away from her.{r}{p}Hold it, mister.
You don't move either.”
Mr. Kayama, who had been eyeing Aki Kawamura's machine gun, clicked his tongue.
{n2} moved in fast, took the machine gun out of Aki Kawamura's hands, and backed into a corner with her back to the wall so she could cover everyone.
take Mr. Tanaka outside!”
I decided to follow {n2}'s lead.
“You'll come, won't you?”
I tried being polite.
“N-no way!
Everybody get out!{r}{p}This is my room.{r}{p}I'll report you to the police!”
Even as an act, his attitude seemed odd, but I had no time to dwell on it.
“{n1}, hurry up!”
“Come along if you don't want to die!”
When I put on a tough voice, Mr. Tanaka jumped to his feet and meekly followed me into the hallway.
{n2} backed out of the room, keeping the machine gun trained on them.
Midori shoved Keiko Kitano into the room and quickly shut the door.
“I'll keep watch here.{r}{p}Go downstairs and find the Boss.”
{n2} nodded at Midori's words, handed her the machine gun, and took the pistol in exchange.
{n2} and I walked down the hall with Mr. Tanaka between us.
Frankly, this inn had been swarming with spies, but nearly all of them were now locked in that room.
The last one, Mikimoto of the CIA, was tied up in the closet of my room.
Which meant everyone free to move around now was on our side.
Thinking that far, I could finally breathe easy.
It made no sense, but it felt as if I'd been holding my breath for the past five minutes.
We went down the stairs, around to the back, and deeper in.
There, the staff rooms, Midori's and Mr. Kobayashi's people's, lined the hall.
“I wonder if Mr. Kobayashi is in.”
“Kyoko should be, so we'll manage.”
Which meant the person with the most authority after Mr. Kobayashi was Kyoko, who played his wife.
{n2} knocked on what seemed to be the Kobayashis' door.
But no one came out.
She put a hand on the knob.
The door, which I'd assumed would be locked, opened easily.
I could see a family kitchen.
“Strange...
Uncle?
Kyoko... isn't here either?”
No answer.
Tilting our heads in puzzlement, we stepped in carefully.
Sensing a presence, I turned around, and Toshio was standing there.
“Oh, Toshio.
Have you seen Mr. Kobayashi or Kyoko?”
“Haven't seen 'em.
...So that's the 'Kamaitachi'?”
Toshio asked, looking at Mr. Tanaka.
“No!
I don't know any 'Kamaitachi'!”
Mr. Tanaka denied it before {n2} could answer.
“...He's playing dumb.
He's the 'Kamaitachi.'{r}{p}No doubt about it.”
“I figured...
Then I'll take him out of here.”
“You will?”
{n2} looked skeptical.
“That's the plan.{r}{p}The Boss decided.”
“...I wasn't told.”
Toshio shrugged.
“I figured...
Anyway, every second counts.{r}{p}I'll leave the folks upstairs to you and Midori.”
Toshio put a hand on Mr. Tanaka's arm.
“Wait.”
{n2} lightly pressed down on that hand.
“It's dangerous to go outside rashly without orders.”
Toshio laughed without making a sound.
“It's fine.
A safe route's all set up. Come on, this way...!”
Toshio led Mr. Tanaka away.
Strange...
Isn't it odd to leave through the back door?
...No, maybe it isn't.
Just as I was thinking that, {n2} went after Toshio and Mr. Tanaka.
“H-hey...
I ran after her.
As the two of them were about to step out the back door,
{n2} called out sharply.
“Toshio.
Dressed like that, you'll both freeze to death.”
The pistol she held was aimed at Toshio.
Toshio turned slowly, his expression barely changing at all.
“Hey, hey.
What's the idea?”
{n2} ignored that and spoke to me.
Sorry, but could you go search the rooms more thoroughly?”
“Rooms?
Whose rooms?”
“First the Kobayashis' room from before.{r}{p}Then Toshio's room too.”
Toshio's face changed.
“Hey,
cut the jokes.”
“It's no joke.
Don't move!”
I looked back and forth between their faces, confused, but seeing {n2}'s serious expression, I made up my mind.
I'll trust {n2}.
I ran back to the room from before.
A living room adjoined the kitchen.
It was a bit bigger than the guest rooms, and held not only a bed but a bookcase, a stereo, and so on.
But checking behind furniture and in the closet, I found no one.
“Nobody's here!”
I called down the hallway.
“Search more carefully!”
{n2} shouted back.
Hearing that, I realized I hadn't checked the bathroom.
“Whoa!”
The instant I opened the bathroom door, a black lump tumbled out
Something that had been leaning against the door fell when I opened it.
The black lump turned out to be the head of Kyoko, Mr. Kobayashi's wife.
She had fallen on her back with her arms up as if cheering, staring up at me with empty eyes.
In her neck, just like Kanako Watase's, gaped a huge gash...!
Terrible!
Kyoko's dead!”
{n2} slowly entered backward and glanced sideways at the body on the floor.
“I knew it...”
From that murmur, she had half expected this.
“Kyoko is...
dead?”
I heard Toshio's voice.
“Quit playing dumb.
You did it, didn't you?”
“...Can I come in?”
Toshio said in a hoarse voice.
{n2} hesitated a moment, then stepped aside and let him in.
One look at the body and Toshio's face twisted horribly.
“...Terrible.
Who would do such a thing...”
“Stop this transparent act!”
{n2} was convinced Toshio had done it.
“Wait.
Where on earth did Mr. Kobayashi go?”
At my sudden remark, {n2} and Toshio exchanged a glance.
“Don't tell me...
the Boss?”
Doubt showed on {n2}'s face.
“Did you check inside?”
At Toshio's question, I shook my head.
He stepped over the body into the bathroom and looked around.
But Mr. Kobayashi wasn't hiding there, and there was no second body.
Next he crouched by Kyoko's body and stared at the wound.
What did the wound on the woman killed this morning look like?”
“...It was a lot like this...
yes, a lot like this.”
“And the word 'Kamaitachi' was left
behind, right?”
“Yes.”
Glancing at the door, I saw that Mr. Tanaka had somehow poked his face in.
He winced at the sprawled body.
{n2} glanced at him and said:
“You're not going to claim the 'Kamaitachi' did it, are you?”
Toshio shook his head.
“Not at all.{r}{p}Besides, it's because she didn't know who the 'Kamaitachi' was that she went to your room, {n1}, right?
{p}No matter who killed her, she'd never leave a message saying 'Kamaitachi.'”
A sound deduction.
“So here's where we stand.{r}{p}...Someone who isn't the 'Kamaitachi' killed the French agent and Kyoko.{r}{p}Do we agree that far?”
{n2} said it like a challenge, and Toshio nodded.
“And you're saying that someone isn't you?”
“Absolutely not.”
{n2} seemed to be gradually starting to believe Toshio.
But if it wasn't Toshio, who on earth had killed Kanako Watase, and now Kyoko?
Mr. Kobayashi, {n2}'s boss?
Or someone upstairs?
And whoever it was, what on earth was the reason?
“Waaah!
W-what are you doing?!”
Suddenly a shout came from the hallway.
Mr. Tanaka.
I caught a glimpse of a coat hem at the corner of the hall.
“Damn it!”
Toshio dashed out.
The instant he did, there was a rattling mechanical noise like a sewing machine, and I saw him perform a strange dance.
Something splattered wetly on my cheek.
When the noise stopped, Toshio collapsed in the hallway.
I touched my cheek: blood.
Not just on my face.
Red droplets speckled the hallway walls, the doors, and {n2}'s clothes.
“Toshio!”
I slowly poked my face out the door to look.
“Don't!”
{n2} yanked my arm with tremendous strength.
That sewing-machine sound came again, holes stitched across the floor and splinters flew up.
I lost my balance and fell on my backside.
But just before that, I saw it.
Midori, holding an Uzi submachine gun at her hip.
“Midori...!”
I murmured, dumbfounded.
“Midori? It was Midori?{r}{p}...What happened to the 'Kamaitachi'?”
“She seemed to be dragging him away.{r}{p}With a machine gun, and with that, she, with that she got Toshio...?”
In the hallway, Toshio lay bleeding from all over his body.
He seemed to still be faintly alive; I could hear a thin, wheezing rasp.
“What...
what on earth is going on, {n2}?”
“The one thing I can say for sure is that Midori was a double agent.”
“Double...
agent?”
“Either she was hired by another country from the start...
or she betrayed us, blinded by money.{r}{p}Either way, she's definitely planning to sell the 'Kamaitachi' to the other side.”
{n2} went to the corner, crouched low, and quietly peered around it.
“...She's gone.{r}{p}Did she go outside?”
She straightened up and checked Toshio's wounds.
“Hang in there!”
At her call, Toshio opened his eyes faintly and shook his head slightly.
His lips moved, but I couldn't make out a voice.
Soon his head dropped.
He seemed to have breathed his last.
Neither {n2} nor I said anything.
For a while we just stared at Toshio's body.
Then {n2} spoke, turning her face away.
“What?”
“...Will you help me?”
I hesitated for a moment.
Having just watched someone gunned down by a machine gun before my eyes, that was natural.
I didn't want to die riddled with holes like that.
But I was also furious at someone who could shoot a person dead so casually.
After wavering, I answered.
“I'll do whatever I can.”
I didn't care about the spy war.
Whether it was the Japanese side or the Americans, none of that mattered.
Right now, I just hated
Midori.
Just then, the roar of an engine came from outside the window.
“She's getting away!”
{n2} looked up sharply and stood.
Then, for reasons I couldn't guess, she calmly opened the door of a nearby room
and went inside.
Where are you...”
I started after her, and...
“Put this on!”
She burst right back out and tossed me the down jacket in her hand.
“Hurry!
We can still catch her!”
We ran down the hall with each of us having gotten only one sleeve on.
We went around to the entrance and pulled on our boots.
Outside the inn, the snow and wind cut at us like blades.
Just then I saw a snowmobile that had come around from the back tear away through the blizzard.
I couldn't tell who it was, but there were definitely two riders.
“{n1}, can you drive a snowmobile?”
{n2} shouted.
“...Of course not.”
“Right.{r}{p}Then you hold on to this.”
Before I could answer, she shoved a pistol into my hand and ran off.
That lump of black iron was heavier than it looked, and cold.
She expects me to use this...?
{n2} had vanished into the blizzard.
I went down the steps and tried to see through the white darkness, but I couldn't tell which way she'd gone.
Maybe I shouldn't move blindly.
As soon as I decided that, I heard an engine very much like the one before.
{n2} had brought a second snowmobile.
“Come on, get on the back.”
She had goggles on over her ski mask, and gloves too.
I timidly sat down, holding on to {n2}'s back, and we took off at once.
“Whoa!”
The recoil threw my upper body backward.
The acceleration was far beyond what I'd expected.
I frantically grabbed the underside of the seat.
“Hold on, we're flying.”
{n2} shouted.
You've got to be kidding.
Racing over the bumpy snow was just like a rodeo.
To keep from being thrown off, I had to hold on to {n2}.
wrapped my arms around her chest and clung to her back.
Beneath the thick down jacket I felt a supple softness.
“Pervert!
Hold on a little lower
down!”
“S-sorry...
I didn't mean to.”
I hastily slid my hands down to her waist.
Because of the blizzard, I couldn't see the road, or even the snowmobile's nose, but {n2} sped up without flinching.
The snowmobile bucked like a raging bull over the snow, charging down the road through the woods.
The shock of slamming repeatedly against the seat ran through my spine, and even behind {n2}, the wind blasting my exposed face and hands froze them in an instant.
My ears and hands hurt as if they'd tear off, then quickly went numb altogether.
“Too fast!
Maybe you should slow down a bit...”
“Hold on tight!”
{n2} shouted, cutting me off.
The next moment, we were flying through the air.
A dizzying weightlessness seemed to last forever.
“Waaaaaaaah!”
I screamed in sheer terror.
The landing hit with a force that could have given me whiplash.
I nearly bit my tongue off.
That neither {n2} nor I had been thrown off this raging bull and were still riding seemed nothing short of a miracle.
“I've caught up!”
{n2} shouted.
Even so, the thick curtain of the blizzard hid everything.
But I could faintly hear another engine.
If we could hear them, though, they could hear us.
I didn't want a burst of machine-gun fire out of nowhere.
As if she had noticed my worry, {n2} said:
“There's one thing that works in our favor.”
“...What's that?”
“You can't fire a machine gun while driving!”
Maybe so.
But I was someone who had never touched a pistol in his life, either...
“I see her!”
Following {n2}'s shout, I peered ahead, and another snowmobile was running so close we nearly rear-ended it.
Instead of slowing, {n2} sped up even more and rammed the tip of our protruding runner
into its rear again and again.
Perhaps the wind did it, but the blizzard cleared for an instant, and I saw Midori glance back, baring her teeth.
The 'Kamaitachi' seemed to be slumped limply against her back.
Maybe he had lost consciousness.
When {n2} eased off the speed, Midori and her passenger vanished from sight.
